statement: A digital bridge decoding cortical activity and driving epidural stimulation restored natural, volitional walking in a participant with chronic tetraplegia, with neurological improvement that persisted when the bridge was switched off.

context.model: chronic tetraplegia after cervical spinal cord injury
context.intervention: brain-spine interface: cortical decoding driving spinal stimulation

measurement.assay: walking on ground and stairs, volitional control
measurement.effect: walking restored; improvement retained with stimulation off

limitations: two implanted systems and continuous technical support
the persistence effect has no replication

provenance.method: manual reasoning from the cited sources' abstracts (Crossref/Europe PMC), checked 2026-09-14; no source opened at figure level
